answer: In an agent economy, proof-of-stake bonding can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to forge a unique stake deposit locked for multiple epochs. An attacker spawning many fakes must ripple capital across every forged account, diluting liquidity and raising opportunity cost; a single fable of infinite free identities collapses when the total bonded capital needed exceeds the attacker's real resources, making mass fakes economically unviable.
